text: dsh-plugin-greet 是一款 DeepSeek Harness 工具插件：它通过注入 tools 服务注册模型可调用的 greet 工具，为指定姓名生成中文或英文问候。用户可选择友好或正式语气，也可设置默认语言、默认风格、英文问候词和标点；工具校验并清理输入姓名，返回包含问候文本及规范化参数的结构化结果。适合希望让 DSH 按指定语言和语气生成个性化问候的用户。安装到 DSH profile 后即可使用，不需要额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-plugin-greet registers a DSH greet tool for English or Chinese greetings in friendly or formal styles. Users can configure defaults and English wording. It trims and validates names, then returns readable text and structured fields. No API key or external service is needed.
让 DSH 用中文正式地向指定姓名问好。
有没有能根据名字生成英文问候语的工具？
我想让助手用亲切语气欢迎某个人。
DSH 能不能按我给的姓名说您好？
如何调整默认问候风格和英文开场词？
我需要一种能输出中文亲切问候的 DSH 工具。
Can DSH greet a person by name in a formal tone?
I want the assistant to produce a friendly greeting in Chinese.
dsh-plugin-greet 的功能「多语言问候」：根据输入姓名生成中文或英文问候，并可选择亲切或正式语气。模型调用 greet 工具时传入姓名以及可选的语言、风格，插件返回问候文字。
dsh-plugin-greet 的功能「默认值配置」：设置默认语言、默认风格、英文问候词和标点。安装配置中传入这些字段后，模型省略语言或风格时使用相应默认值，友好英文输出也采用设定的问候词和标点。
dsh-plugin-greet 的功能「结构化问候结果」：greet 工具除可读问候文本外，也返回姓名、语言和风格字段。模型调用工具后，渲染器将结果转换为纯文本问候，其他工具逻辑可使用结构化字段。
dsh-plugin-greet README · Introduction：

dsh-plugin-greet README · dsh-plugin-greet：English | [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md)

A beginner-friendly, installable DeepSeek Harness plugin that demonstrates bundle distribution, profile composition, plugin configuration, the typed `defineTool()` API, structured output, validation, testing, and a real model-driven tool call.

> This is a community example, not an official DeepSeek AI plugin. DeepSeek Harness is currently in Developer Preview, so future releases may require compatibility updates.

dsh-plugin-greet README · What you will learn：This repository keeps the implementation in one small entry file so that a new plugin author can follow the complete path:

```text
User prompt
  → model chooses the greet tool
  → argument schema checks the shape
  → execute validates and normalizes values

The example covers:

dsh-plugin-greet README · What you will learn：- exporting a validated plugin `Config`
- injecting and using the Harness `tools` service
- registering a tool with the current `defineTool()` schema DSL
- required and optional tool arguments
- English and Chinese greetings
- friendly and formal styles
- structured canonical output with a text renderer
- actionable validation errors
- unit tests and CI packaging checks
dsh-plugin-greet README · Tool contract：The plugin registers one model-callable tool named `greet`.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Input：| Field | Required | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Yes | Non-empty string, at most 80 characters | — |
| `language` | No | `en`, `zh` | Plugin configuration |
| `style` | No | `friendly`, `formal` | Plugin configuration |

Leading and trailing whitespace is removed from `name`. Unknown arguments, empty names, unsupported languages, and unsupported styles are rejected with clear errors.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Output：The canonical result is structured data:

```json
{
  "message": "Hello, Ada!",
  "name": "Ada",
  "language": "en",

`output.render` converts that value into the model-facing text:

```text
Hello, Ada!
```

This separation lets other plugins or policies use the structured fields without making the model read raw JSON.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Greeting examples：| Language | Style | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | Friendly | `Hello, Ada!` |
| English | Formal | `Greetings, Ada.` |
| Chinese | Friendly | `你好，小明！` |
| Chinese | Formal | `您好，小明。` |

dsh-plugin-greet README · Supported dsh versions：For `dsh-plugin-greet@0.3.5`, use **`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5`**. The preview **`0.2.2-alpha.2`** is also verified. Compatibility is stated for these exact releases, not all `0.2.x` versions.

Last checked: **November 1, 2026**.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Supported dsh versions：Current CI covers dsh `0.2.1-rc.5` on Node.js 22.19 and 24, and dsh `0.2.2-alpha.2` on Node.js 24.9 and 24: unit tests, installation of the packed plugin through the profile CLI, four greeting modes, invalid arguments, Web startup, launch-token login, and HTML responses. It does not include a real model request. See the [CI results](https://github.com/0lidaxiang/dsh-plugin-greet/actions).

dsh-plugin-greet README · Supported dsh versions：The old Harness `0.1.2-rc.1` and `0.1.5-alpha.1` releases use broad upstream dependency ranges that can now resolve incompatible services. Their fresh-install failures do not prove the greeting implementation is incompatible with an already-installed old environment; those existing environments were not revalidated. For new installations, use one of the two supported releases above.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Supported dsh versions：The `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` peer declaration retains historical ranges for existing installations. A version satisfying that declaration is not by itself a tested dsh compatibility guarantee. New Harness releases need another compatibility check before being added to the supported list.

To use the verified preview, replace `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5` with `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-alpha.2` consistently in the installation and launch commands below.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Install from npm：For dsh `0.2.1-rc.5`, use Node.js `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0`; the `0.2.2-alpha.2` preview requires `>=24.9.0`. Install pnpm (`npm install -g pnpm@10.32.1`) for profile plugin management. Development dependencies target Harness `0.2.1-rc.5`; CI also verifies `0.2.2-alpha.2`. The commands below pin the default release tested by this repository.

Stop any running DeepSeek Harness instance, then install the package into the `web` profile:

dsh-plugin-greet README · Install from npm：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-greet@0.3.5
```

Version `0.3.3` updates the compatibility declarations required by newer Harness installers and adapts the test harness to the preview's separate tool executor and batch API. Its greeting behavior is unchanged from `0.3.0`.

This command does more than a regular `npm install`: it installs the package into the selected Harness profile and adds its declared bundle to the profile composition.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Install from npm：Before starting, confirm that the bundle is present in the final configuration:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 --profile web --dump-config
```

Then start the Web UI:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web
```

dsh-plugin-greet README · Try the tool：Use the page opened by the launcher, or open the complete URL printed in the terminal, including its `?token=...` query. The default port is 3080. The first visit establishes a browser session and redirects to the clean URL; opening the bare address without a valid session returns 401. Then send:

```text
You must use the greet tool to greet Ada in a friendly English style.
```

The expected tool call is:

```text
IN  { "name": "Ada", "language": "en", "style": "friendly" }
OUT Hello, Ada!
```

dsh-plugin-greet README · Try the tool：Try Chinese formal output:

```text
You must use the greet tool to greet 小明 in formal Chinese.
```

Expected result:

```text
IN  { "name": "小明", "language": "zh", "style": "formal" }
OUT 您好，小明。
```

The plugin does not listen for keywords such as `Hello`. It makes the tool available to the model, and the model decides whether to call it. Explicitly naming the `greet` tool makes the behavior easier to verify.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Configure the plugin：The exported configuration schema supplies these defaults:

```yaml
greeting: Hello
punctuation: "!"
defaultLanguage: en
defaultStyle: friendly

To override them, restate the plugin row in a later patch layer, such as the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: greet-tool
      name: dsh-plugin-greet
      config:

With that configuration, a call containing only `{ "name": "Grace" }` returns `Hi, Grace!`.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Configure the plugin：`greeting` and `punctuation` customize friendly English output. Chinese and formal wording use the built-in examples shown above. `defaultLanguage` and `defaultStyle` are used only when the model omits those arguments.

Later patch layers replace the entire row configuration rather than deep-merging individual keys, so keep `id`, `name`, and the complete desired `config` together.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Install from GitHub：To install the current development branch:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add \
  github:0lidaxiang/dsh-plugin-greet#master
```

For stable usage, prefer a published npm version, release tag, or specific commit SHA.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Install from a local checkout：Run this command from the parent directory of the repository:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-greet
```

After changing the code, restart DeepSeek Harness and verify the tool through the chat interface.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Develop and test：Install dependencies and run the unit tests:

```sh
npm ci
npm test
```

Run the complete local check, including the npm package preview:

```sh
npm run check
```

The test suite imports the real Harness tool API and verifies configuration defaults, registration metadata, all four greeting modes, structured output rendering, whitespace normalization, invalid values, unknown arguments, and length limits. GitHub Actions runs these checks on Node.js 22.19 and 24.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Develop and test：Run the same compatibility checks as CI (requires pnpm and registry access):

```sh
npm run test:compat -- 0.2.1-rc.5
npm run test:compat -- 0.2.2-alpha.2 # Node.js >=24.9.0
```

dsh-plugin-greet README · Develop and test：Each check installs the selected Harness into a temporary directory, runs the unit tests against it, packs this checkout, installs that tarball through the real profile CLI, and starts Web on an available loopback port. It verifies all four greetings, invalid arguments, the launch-token login flow, and the HTML response, then stops the server and removes the temporary profile. It does not call a model or use your existing profile. CI uses the version combinations listed in the compatibility section. Installation enforces the host's Node engine requirement.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Develop and test：Update Cordis alongside the Harness development packages: `0.2.1-rc.5` requires Cordis `~4.0.5`, while `0.2.2-alpha.2` requires `~4.0.6-alpha.1`. The compatibility script reads the selected release's Cordis peer requirement from the official npm registry instead of reusing the development version. Pin matching versions of `dsh-tools` and `dsh-system-prompt`; the `dsh-tools` npm `latest` tag does not track the CLI's `latest` tag.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Develop and test：Standalone tests for `0.2.2-alpha.2` mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-executor-native` and use the batch `tools.execute({ calls, signal })` API. The normal Web profile already supplies its executor; the plugin itself still only registers `greet`. The Web probe uses the host's executor without adding one.

After publishing, verify installation from npm instead of the local tarball:

```sh
npm run test:compat -- 0.2.1-rc.5 --published
```
dsh-plugin-greet README · Publish with OIDC：For the maintainer release procedure, see [Releasing dsh-plugin-greet](docs/releasing.md).

dsh-plugin-greet README · Publish with OIDC：The `Publish npm package` GitHub Actions workflow first checks npm 12 default-policy installation, plugin compatibility, and real terminal input/output. Run it with `publish=false` to rehearse without publishing. To release, bump the package and lockfile version, push the matching `vX.Y.Z` tag, then dispatch from that tag with `publish=true`. The protected `npm-publish` job publishes the verified tarball using OIDC, without a stored npm write token.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Publish with OIDC：The npm trusted publisher for `dsh-plugin-greet` must authorize GitHub repository `0lidaxiang/dsh-plugin-greet`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `npm-publish`, and direct `npm publish`. Existing users do not need to reinstall or change their configuration for this publishing setup.
dsh-plugin-greet README · The model replies but does not call `greet`：Say explicitly: `You must use the greet tool...`. A normal greeting such as `Hello` does not force a tool call.
section: The model replies but does not call `greet`

text: dsh-plugin-greet README · The tool is not listed：Stop the running Harness process, reinstall the plugin into the same profile, inspect `--dump-config`, and then restart the Web UI.

dsh-plugin-greet README · `npm install dsh-plugin-greet` worked, but the tool is missing：A regular npm install only adds a dependency to the current Node.js project. Use `dsh plugin --profile <name> add ...` to install and compose the bundle into a Harness profile.
section: `npm install dsh-plugin-greet` worked, but the tool is missing

text: dsh-plugin-greet README · The Web page returns 401：Open the complete launch URL printed by the current Harness process, including `?token=...`, to establish a browser session. An old process's token or a bare URL in a browser without a valid session will not log you in.

dsh-plugin-greet README · Installation reports a missing Harness peer：The official profile disables automatic peer installation and resolves Harness services from the host at startup, so pnpm can report a missing peer during installation. Check the supported versions above, inspect `--dump-config`, and restart Harness. Avoid adding a separate copy of `dsh-tools` to the profile to silence this warning; the plugin should use the host's service.
section: Installation reports a missing Harness peer

text: dsh-plugin-greet README · Installation is rejected as incompatible：Newer Harness versions enforce the declared `dsh-tools` peer range. Upgrade to `dsh-plugin-greet@0.3.5` for the versions in the current compatibility table. A missing-peer warning during pnpm installation is different from Harness rejecting an unsupported version. For other dsh releases, verify compatibility before adding them to the declaration.
dsh-plugin-greet README · My configuration did not take effect：Make sure your later patch restates the row with the same `id` (`greet-tool`), the package `name`, and the complete `config` object.
section: My configuration did not take effect

dsh-plugin-greet README · Security and compatibility：DeepSeek Harness plugins run inside the host process. Review third-party plugin source code before installation, and prefer a pinned release tag or commit SHA.

The plugin has no network, filesystem, shell, or credential access. It uses the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` package for typed tool registration and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` for configuration validation.
